title: Structural quality gate catches table/code-block loss

ISO country codes page: 249-row data table stripped despite include_tables=True (trafilatura output 96% of page text but zero table data). Python docs: code blocks flattened into inline text. Add tests for both table-loss and code-loss detection 6. Smoke test against ISO country codes page and Python asyncio docs
brief.done: ISO country codes page produces output containing table data (country names and codes). Python asyncio docs produce output with fenced code blocks. Cascade falls through to Readability when trafilatura drops structure. Existing pages (Wikipedia article, ONS, HN) unaffected.

title: capture verb records network requests during a passe script

brief.why: passe has zero use of the CDP Network domain. chrome-log is a daemon that watches all tabs. There's a gap: planned, single-tab, ephemeral network capture during a script — 'goto URL, do stuff, show me what API calls it made.' Useful for reverse-engineering SPAs without running the always-on daemon.
brief.what: 1. Add capture verb that enables Network.enable on passe's tab 2. Buffer Network.requestWillBeSent and Network.responseReceived events during the script 3. At end of script (or on explicit capture-stop), write collected requests to JSONL file 4. Include method, URL, status, headers, timing 5. Optional: capture response bodies (large — make opt-in) 6. Consider capture-start/capture-stop pair vs whole-script capture 7. Keep it ephemeral — no daemon, no multi-tab
brief.done: passe run -c 'capture /tmp/reqs.jsonl; goto https://spa.example.com; click .search; wait 2000' produces a JSONL file of all network requests made during the script. Response bodies opt-in via --bodies flag.

brief.why: Research tasks often need to read an entire docs site. The Utiq session required discovering the nav tree via snapshot, manually extracting URLs, then visiting each one sequentially — 10 separate passe calls. A crawl verb would automate this common pattern.
brief.what: 1. Add crawl verb: crawl <url> [--depth N] [--same-domain] [--selector css] <output-dir> 2. Visits the starting URL, discovers links (optionally filtered by CSS selector for nav elements), follows them to --depth (default 1) 3. Deposits one markdown file per page in output-dir, named by URL slug 4. Respects --same-domain to avoid following external links 5. Uses the fetch pipeline internally (auto-wait + read cascade) 6. Reports summary: pages found, pages read, pages skipped, total time 7. Consider parallelising page reads (open multiple tabs? or sequential but fast with auto-wait)
brief.done: passe run -c 'crawl https://docs.utiq.com/docs/utiq-technology --depth 1 --same-domain /tmp/utiq-docs/' produces one markdown file per linked docs page. Completes in under 10 seconds for a 10-page site.

title: outerHTML includes shadow DOM content — extractors see the full page

brief.why: document.documentElement.outerHTML skips shadow root content. MDN uses <mdn-code-example> web components with code inside shadow DOM — 17 code examples (8KB) invisible to both trafilatura and Readability. Any site using web components loses content silently.
brief.what: 1. Write a JS flattener function that walks the DOM tree, finds elements with .shadowRoot, and inlines shadow root children into the light DOM before serialization 2. Replace the do_eval('document.documentElement.outerHTML') call in do_read with the flattener 3. Test against MDN Promise page — should recover all 17 code examples (8191 chars) 4. Test against regular pages (Wikipedia, ONS) — flattener must not break non-shadow-DOM pages 5. Test performance — flattening adds DOM walking overhead, measure on a heavy page
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto MDN_PROMISE_URL; read /tmp/out.md' produces markdown with fenced code blocks from shadow DOM. grep -c backtick-fence returns >0. Regular pages unaffected. No performance regression >100ms.

title: Replace Readability.js primary path with trafilatura cascade

brief.why: read only works on articles. Trafilatura handles any page type and produces better markdown with tables, code blocks, and links. Chrome gives us the rendered DOM; trafilatura cleans it server-side.
brief.what: 1. Add trafilatura to pyproject.toml dependencies 2. Refactor do_read: get outerHTML + innerText length from Chrome via eval, run trafilatura.extract with include_formatting=True on Python side 3. If trafilatura returns None or too short, fall back to current Readability.js+Turndown path 4. If Readability also fails, fall back to innerText (existing behaviour) 5. Keep ratio warning system — compare trafilatura output length vs page innerText length 6. Update tests — mock the new flow, test cascade fallback 7. Update CLAUDE.md — read is no longer articles-only 8. Reinstall and smoke test against my.itv.com
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto URL; read /tmp/out.md' uses trafilatura as primary extractor. Falls back to Readability then innerText. Tests pass. my.itv.com hub page produces clean markdown.
